context: Evaluates: Separate Business Logic from a Fat Controller

checklist.name: Controller is thin: order-controller.ts contains no
checklist.description: **Controller is thin**: `order-controller.ts` contains no business logic — it extracts `req.body` fields and delegates to the use case, then formats the HTTP response

checklist.name: Business logic moved to use case:
checklist.description: **Business logic moved to use case**: `place-order.ts` contains the inventory validation, price calculation, order creation, and email notification logic

checklist.name: Use case has no HTTP imports:
checklist.description: **Use case has no HTTP imports**: `place-order.ts` does not import from `express` and does not accept `Request` or `Response` parameters

checklist.name: Use case accepts typed input: place-order.ts
checklist.description: **Use case accepts typed input**: `place-order.ts` function accepts a typed input (`userId` and `items`) rather than the raw HTTP request object

checklist.name: Same observable behavior preserved: The controller
checklist.description: **Same observable behavior preserved**: The controller still returns 400 on insufficient stock and 201 with `orderId` and `total` on success
